reading.body:
Three open roles in privacy and data protection at AI companies is too small a sample to describe a hiring trend.

The listings are all at AI developers: Harvey in Dublin, OpenAI in San Francisco, and Figure in San Jose. Two are tagged as AI roles and one as security, but all three carry the same function, privacy and data protection. Two are remote, which for legal and research privacy work suggests the constraint is expertise rather than location.

What the data does not show is volume. Three postings cannot distinguish a growing compliance function from routine backfill, and there is no comparison point from earlier periods. The sources listed include aggregators and federal job boards, but none of their listings appear here, so the count reflects direct company career boards only.

Nothing in this data speaks to compute, buildings, or power. Privacy hiring is driven by regulation and data handling, not by the physical constraints that bind AI scaling.

The three postings split across two categories, ai and security, but converge on one function. That means the function tag, not the category tag, is what actually groups these roles. A reader filtering by category would see two AI jobs and one security job and miss that all three are the same kind of hire.

Two of the three are remote, and the two remote ones are the legal and research roles at Harvey and OpenAI. The one on-site role is the program manager at Figure in San Jose. The pattern the data supports is that the individual-contributor privacy roles are location-flexible while the coordination role is not, though three postings is a thin basis for that claim.

All three come from company career boards, Greenhouse and Ashby, and none from the aggregators or federal boards in the source list. The count of three is therefore a floor set by which boards this page reads, not a measure of the market. The same source list includes Indeed Hiring Lab and InfoSec Job Board as market-data trackers, which are a different kind of source than a job posting and would not add to the count even if consulted.

What does "Privacy and Data Protection" hiring at AI companies look like right now?

Three postings appear in this data, at Harvey, OpenAI, and Figure. That is the entire count, and it is too small to call a trend.

Are these roles remote or on-site?

Two are remote, the Harvey counsel role and the OpenAI research engineer role. The Figure program manager role is on-site in San Jose.

Which companies are hiring for this function?

Harvey, OpenAI, and Figure. Harvey's role is in Dublin, OpenAI's in San Francisco, and Figure's in San Jose.

Why do these jobs not appear on the aggregator sites listed as sources?

The data does not say. The source list includes Adzuna, Jooble, Remotive, Remote OK, Arbeitnow, The Muse, USAJobs, and the company career boards, but only the career boards, Greenhouse and Ashby, produced the three listings shown.

Is privacy hiring at AI companies growing?

The data cannot answer this. There is no earlier period to compare against and only three postings in the current snapshot.

Do these roles relate to compute, data centers, or power constraints?

No. Nothing in this data connects privacy and data protection hiring to compute, buildings, or power.
